subject: Criminology
question_text: In penology, the rehabilitative model of punishment primarily aims to:
option_a: Reform the offender and prepare him for lawful life in society
option_b: Inflict pain equal to the harm caused by the crime
option_c: Permanently remove dangerous persons from society
option_d: Create public fear to prevent future offences
explanation_detailed: Rehabilitation treats crime partly as a social and personal problem that can be corrected through education, training, and counseling. Pakistani prison reform debates often stress vocational training and aftercare because the long-term goal is to reduce reoffending after release.

subject: Criminology
question_text: Under the Probation of Offenders Ordinance, 1960, probation in Pakistan generally means:
option_a: Release after serving the full sentence in prison
option_b: Supervised freedom in the community instead of imprisonment in suitable cases
option_c: Automatic acquittal without any court supervision
option_d: Transfer of the offender to a foreign correctional facility
explanation_detailed: Probation allows a court to release an offender on conditions such as good behavior and reporting to authorities rather than sending him to jail. It is a key non-custodial measure in Pakistan's correctional system for minor and first-time offenders.

option_d: Acquittal due to lack of evidence
explanation_detailed: Recidivism is one of the main tests of whether prisons, probation, and aftercare programs are working. High reoffending rates push policymakers toward rehabilitation, parole reform, and community-based correction.

subject: Criminology
question_text: Which statement best distinguishes parole from probation?
option_a: Probation is ordered by the court before imprisonment, while parole is early release from prison under supervision
option_b: Parole is always given at the time of conviction without any supervision
option_c: Probation applies only after the full prison term has been completed
option_d: Parole and probation are identical processes under Pakistani law
explanation_detailed: Probation is usually a sentencing alternative decided by the court, whereas parole is granted after part of a prison sentence has been served. Both involve supervision in the community, but they begin at different stages of the criminal justice process.

subject: Criminology
question_text: The Prisons Act, 1894, which still forms the basic legal framework for prisons in Pakistan, was originally enacted during:
explanation_detailed: The Prisons Act, 1894, is colonial-era legislation that continues to govern many prison administration matters in Pakistan. Students should note that modern reform efforts often seek to update this old framework with human rights and rehabilitation standards.

subject: Criminology
question_text: Open prisons or open colonies in penology are mainly designed to:
option_a: House only condemned prisoners awaiting execution
option_b: Allow selected inmates greater freedom, work, and movement to ease reintegration
option_c: Replace all courts with prison-based tribunals
option_d: Punish the most violent offenders through strict isolation
explanation_detailed: Open prisons use minimum security because inmates selected for them are considered low risk and near release. The idea is to build self-discipline, employment habits, and social adjustment before full return to society.

option_b: Repairing harm by involving the victim, offender, and community
option_c: Permanent exclusion of the offender from society
explanation_detailed: Restorative justice focuses on accountability and making amends, not only on state punishment. It seeks to restore relationships and reduce future conflict by addressing the needs of victims and communities as well as offenders.

subject: Criminology
question_text: An indeterminate sentence in penology is one in which:
option_a: The exact period of imprisonment is fixed at the time of conviction
option_b: The offender is never required to serve any custodial term
option_c: Only a fine is imposed and no prison term is possible
option_d: The offender serves a minimum term and release depends on conduct and review
explanation_detailed: Indeterminate sentencing links release to reform, behavior, and supervisory review rather than to a fixed date alone. It reflects the rehabilitative idea that correction should continue until the offender is fit for safe re-entry into society.

subject: Criminology
question_text: Borstal or borstal-type institutions in penology are mainly meant for:
option_b: Young offenders who can still be reformed through training and education
explanation_detailed: Borstal institutions were developed to separate young offenders from hardened adult criminals. The focus is on discipline, education, and vocational skills so that youthful offenders are not permanently damaged by ordinary prison culture.

subject: Criminology
question_text: The theory of incapacitation in penology seeks to prevent crime mainly by:
option_a: Changing the offender's values through counseling
option_c: Physically restricting the offender's ability to commit further offences
option_d: Publishing crime statistics to educate the public
explanation_detailed: Incapacitation works by detention, restraint, or removal from free society so the offender cannot immediately reoffend. Long prison terms and, in extreme cases, the death penalty are often justified under this preventive logic.
